Live imaging of wound closure. MDCK monolayers were maintained in EGM-2 endothelial medium at 37 °C and 5% CO2 and plated in 6-well plates (90% confluence). Where indicated, cells were treated with PF-573228 (1 µM) immediately after wounding. Spheroids formed in ultra-low-attachment plates were embedded in collagen I and invasion into the matrix was followed. Cell division was blocked with 10 µg/ml mitomycin-C. Using phase contrast optics, we imaged each wound at 10-min intervals for 36 h. Each condition was run in triplicate and repeated 3 times. Calibration was 454 nm/px.

For migration experiments, U-2 OS cells were plated at 20000 cells/well in 24-well plates. A linear wound (about 300 um wide) was made across each well with a P200 tip. To exclude proliferation, monolayers were incubated with mitomycin C (10 µg/mL) for 2 h before wounding. CRISPR/Cas9 was used to knock out CDH1, and wounds in these cells were compared with parental controls. Wound closure was followed by transmitted-light time-lapse microscopy every 60 min. Cells between passages 4 and 12 were used. Acquisition used a Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 camera.
